362439.title: Quasisymmetric characteristic formula for a statistic-and-descent model

$$
F_{char}(M;q)=\sum_{x\in X}q^{\operatorname{stat}(x)}F_{\operatorname{set}(x)}.
$$

This is presented as a general form of open conjectures motivated by deforming symmetric-group modules into $\mathcal{H}_n(0)$-modules; the excerpt does not specify additional hypotheses relating $M$ and $X$.

358153.title: The diversity bound for large intersecting families
358153.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}\subset\binom{[n]}{k}$ be an intersecting family, where $n>100k$, and suppose that

$$
|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}.
$$

Here $\varrho(\mathcal{F})$ denotes the diversity of $\mathcal{F}$. **The diversity bound conjecture.** Then

$$
\varrho(\mathcal{F})\geq\frac{3}{7}.
$$

This is posed as a challenging open problem concerning improved lower bounds on the diversity of large intersecting families. Its resolution is left open in the source.

357009.title: Bucko–Czap conjecture on 1-planarity of lexicographic products
357009.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $K_2$ denote the complete graph with two vertices. A graph is **1-planar** if it has a drawing in the plane in which every edge is crossed by at most one other edge. A **cactus** is a connected graph in which every edge belongs to at most one cycle. **Bucko–Czap's conjecture.** The graph $G\circ K_2$ is 1-planar if and only if $G$ is a cactus. This open problem characterizes 1-planarity for lexicographic products with $K_2$ and concerns the relationship between graph substitution and sparse crossing structures.

346829.title: Oboudi's comparability conjecture for trees under independence-polynomial order

$$
T_1\triangleleft T_2\quad\text{or}\quad T_2\trianglelefteq T_1?

The question asks whether every pair of trees of the same order is comparable in this order; the paper presents an infinite family showing that the proposed comparability fails.

343136.title: Finite generation conjecture for verbal subgroups
343136.literal_statement:

**Finite generation conjecture.** If

$$
|G_w|<2^{\aleph_0},
$$

then $w(G)$ is generated by finitely many $w$-values.

339617.title: Diversity bound for intersecting-free hypergraph families
339617.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal F\subset {[n]\choose k}$ satisfy $\nu(\mathcal F)\leq s$ and $n\geq k(s+1)$. Define the $s$-diversity by

$$
\gamma_s(\mathcal F)=\min_T|\mathcal F(\bar T)|,
$$

where $\mathcal F(\bar T)=\\{F\in\mathcal F:F\cap T=\emptyset\\}$. **Diversity bound conjecture.** One has

$$
\gamma_s(\mathcal F)\leq\max\left\\{\sum_{l=2}^{s+1}{{s+1}\choose l}{{n-2s-1}\choose{k-l}},{{(k-1)(s+1)}\choose k}\right\\}.
$$

The conjecture asks for a sharp upper bound on the diversity of a family with matching number at most $s$. The source presents it as a question for further progress; no resolution status is supplied.

340374.title: Mutation connectivity conjecture for uniform matroid polytopes of rank 4
340374.literal_statement:
A **uniform matroid polytope of rank $4$** is a uniform matroid polytope with rank $4$. Consider two such matroid polytopes on the same ground set, and require every intermediate object in a mutation sequence to remain a matroid polytope.

**Mutation connectivity conjecture for uniform matroid polytopes.** Every pair of uniform matroid polytopes of rank $4$ on the same ground set can be transformed into each other by a finite number of mutations, preserving the matroid polytope property.

This problem is motivated by the Cordovil–Las Vergnas conjecture, which asserts mutation connectivity for uniform oriented matroids. The source presents the rank-$4$ matroid-polytope version as an open problem.

329032.title: Collapsibility conjecture for nerve complexes of circular arcs
329032.literal_statement:
Let $l$, $n$, and $k$ be integers satisfying

$$
\frac{l}{l+1}<\frac{k}{n}<\frac{l+1}{l+2}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{N}({n},{k})$ be the nerve complex of the corresponding circular arcs, and let $\partial C_{2l+2}(n)$ denote its embedded sphere.

**Collapsibility conjecture.** The complex $\mathcal{N}({n},{k})$ simplicially collapses to $\partial C_{2l+2}(n)$.

The paper establishes that $\partial C_{2l+2}(n)$ is an embedded sphere whose fundamental class generates the relevant homology group. It remains open whether this embedded sphere is always a combinatorial deformation retract of $\mathcal{N}({n},{k})$; simplicial collapse would imply such a deformation retraction.

388658.title: Extending Pseudosegment Arrangements by Subdivision
388658.literal_statement: How many intersections among an arrangement of pseudosegments in the plane must be added as vertices to allow the pseudosegment arrangment to be extended to a pseudoline arrangement? An arrangement of pseudosegments in the plane is a family of finite-length planar curves such that every two curves intersect in at most one point. An arrangement of pseudolines in the plane is a family of planar curves that extend to infinity on both ends such that every two curves intersect in at most one point. Only some pseudosegment arrangements can be extended to pseudoline arrangements. However, if we allow turning intersection points into vertices of the arrangement, thereby subdividing the segments, then it is always possible to make a pseudosegment arrangement extendible. The question is how many such vertices must be added in the worst-case in terms of the number $n$ of pseudosegments.

317450.title: Compatibility conjecture for the Grossman–Larson coproduct and rooted-tree coproduct
317450.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be the Hopf algebra of rooted trees, let $H_{GL}$ be the Grossman–Larson Hopf algebra, and let $\Delta$ and $S_{GL}$ denote the relevant coproduct and antipode, with $\Delta_{GL}$ the coproduct transported to $H_{GL}$. For a linear map $m^{2,4}$ defined by

$$
m^{2,4}(a\otimes b\otimes c\otimes d)=a\otimes c\otimes bd,
$$

**Compatibility conjecture.** For any rooted tree $t$,

$$
(\Delta_{GL}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal H})\circ\Delta(t)=m^{2,4}\circ(\Delta\otimes\Delta)\circ\Delta_{GL}(t)
$$

and

$$
\Delta\circ S_{GL}(t)=(S_{GL}\otimes\operatorname{id})\circ\Delta(t).
$$

These identities would give an analogue of the corresponding compatibility between the Kreimer and Grossman–Larson structures. The source presents them as a question, so their resolution is not established here.

378640.title: Canonical positive monomial expression conjecture for non-commutative Schur functions
378640.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition of size $k$, and let $s_\lambda({\mathbf u})$ and $h_\lambda({\mathbf u})$ be the non-commutative Schur and homogeneous symmetric functions in the ribbon Schur operators $u_i$. A monomial is written as $\underline{u}=u_{i_k}u_{i_{k-1}}\cdots u_{i_1}$. **Canonical expression conjecture.** The functions $s_\lambda({\mathbf u})$ can be written as a non-negative sum of monomials, with a canonical expression obtained by selecting monomials occurring in $h_\lambda({\mathbf u})$; specifically, the selected monomials satisfy the strict inequalities within each consecutive block of indices determined by the parts of $\lambda$: 

$$
i_{\lambda_1}>i_{\lambda_1-1}>\cdots>i_1,
$$

$$
i_{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}>i_{\lambda_1+\lambda_2-1}>\cdots>i_{\lambda_1+1},
$$

and so on. This is proposed as the paper's main problem and would provide a canonical combinatorial explanation for the non-negativity of the associated skew $q$-Littlewood–Richardson coefficients.

391124.title: Erdős Problem #617 — Missing Colors in Complete-Graph Colorings
391124.literal_statement: Let $r\geq3$. If the edges of the complete graph $K_{r^2+1}$ are colored with $r$ colors, must there exist $r+1$ vertices such that one color is absent from all edges among those vertices? Equivalently, for every finite vertex set $V$ with $|V|=r^2+1$ and every coloring of the unordered pairs of vertices by the colors in $\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, there exist a subset $S\subseteq V$ with $|S|=r+1$ and a color $k$ such that no edge between two distinct vertices of $S$ has color $k$.
